Here is the talk plan cut to the ASTW 2026 contributed slot.

**Event**: ASTW 2026, Chicago — Wednesday Nov 18, 11:20–11:40, Room 2B
**Slot**: 15 min presentation + 5 min Q&A
**Session**: "Anyonic decoherence" — specialist audience
**Title**: "Decoherence pathways in non-Abelian anyonic systems" (as accepted)

The source material is the intro draft (motivation, problem framing) and Section 3 draft with notes (classification, rates, signatures). The letter's Section 2 (model derivation) and Section 4 (platform budget comparison) are not used — the model assumptions are stated bare, and the budget comparison belongs in Q&A if asked.

---

### Presentation structure (9 slides, 15 min)

**Slide 1** (0:30) — Title slide. Title, author, affiliation.

**Slide 2** (1:30) — The gap. Existing analyses treat each decoherence mechanism in isolation, each in its own formalism, at its own protocol stage. What is missing is a classification: which pathways are possible at all, given the algebraic structure of the anyon model and physically motivated restrictions on the environment coupling. The letter supplies that classification.

**Slide 3** (2:30) — The three pathways. Under (A1)–(A4) — gapped bulk, static Markovian environment with local coupling, interferometric readout, fixed positions between adiabatic braids — every decoherence process falls into exactly one of:

- **P1 (fusion-channel dephasing)**: environment correlates with intermediate charge labels while total charge \(a\) is conserved. Suppresses interference, leaves channel populations untouched. Carrier: gapless edge modes.
- **P2 (charge-sector leakage)**: quasiparticle exchange with an external reservoir changes \(a\) itself. Moves state out of \(\mathcal{H}_a\) entirely. Carrier: poisoning from leads, substrate, above-gap excitations.
- **P3 (readout backaction)**: apparatus acquires channel information beyond what the retained record resolves. Vanishes for ideal recorded measurement; grows with record loss and finite-temperature probe imperfections.

**Slide 4** (3:00) — The crossover prediction. P1 rate exponential in bulk depth (Ostrander-Yun: 2–4 μs dephasing at 25 mK within one magnetic length of the edge). P2 rate depth-independent (Braithwaite: ~3.1 s poisoning interval in shielded islands). They cross at \(d^{*} \approx 1.1\ \mu\)m for reference Ising parameters. Beyond \(d^{*}\), the device is leakage-limited, not dephasing-limited. Design consequence: retreating from the edge past \(d^{*}\) buys nothing; engineering effort shifts from geometry to shielding. Finite-size corrections shift \(d^{*}\) by a size-dependent amount but cannot remove the crossing — P1 falls exponentially with depth and P2 does not, at any finite size.

**Slide 5** (2:30) — Readout and the intrinsic floor. Interference visibility factorizes: P1 envelope during traversal × P3 penalty from unrecorded information × intrinsic topological factor set by monodromy of the probe charge with the measured charge. The intrinsic factor is what no engineering recovers: Fibonacci floor \(1/\varphi^{2} \approx 0.38\); Ising \(\sigma\)-probe about a \(\sigma\) charge gives a null fringe — the null itself is the topological signature. Conditioned protocol simulations on Fibonacci: two-crossing braid fidelity 0.91 with records retained, 0.58 with first record discarded — the gap is pure P3 (P1 and P2 held fixed between runs).

**Slide 6** (1:30) — Discriminability. The three pathways are experimentally separable pairwise:
- P1: visibility decays, channel populations stationary.
- P2: telegraph-like jumps in interferometer phase offset, no visibility cost between jumps.
- P3: responds to changes in record retention at fixed hardware.
A device budget resolved along these axes is strictly more informative than a single storage time.

**Slide 7** (1:30) — Scope and limits. The classification is exhaustive within the model assumptions (A1)–(A4). Driven couplings and structured environments are outside the classification as stated. Monotonic decay under P1–P3 is a consequence of (A2): static, memoryless environment — information that leaves the fusion space never returns.

**Slide 8** (1:00) — What the classification predicts for current experiments. Which platform features test each pathway. The crossover depth is a testable, falsifiable prediction for interferometric devices.

**Slide 9** (1:00) — Summary. Decoherence in anyonic media is not a single rate to be minimized but a structured, diagnosable family of processes. The three pathways are identifiable, separable, and carry distinct engineering implications.

---

### Held for Q&A (5 min)

- **Proof of exhaustiveness**: charge split (P = projector onto \(\mathcal{H}_a\)) → channel split via Lindqvist–Mbeku Lemma 2 → P3 as the orthogonal-record-failure (H2-violation) residue. The classification feels inevitable rather than taxonomic.
- **Finite-size corrections**: why they shift \(d^{*}\) but cannot remove the crossing — scaling argument.
- **Platform comparison**: how the budget format (Section 4 of the letter) compares two published platforms along the P1/P2/P3 axes.
- **Stabilizer-formalism contrast**: relationship to surface-code scaling analyses — the classification plays the analogous role for topological hardware that correlated-error decomposition plays for stabilizer codes.
- **Non-Markovian and structured environments**: Nakamura–Chandrasekhar corrections vanish >10\(\xi\) from edge; Oyelaran et al. framework for structured baths — both outside the current classification but natural extensions.
- **Brandão–Weiss einselection**: whether environment-induced superselection in the fusion-channel basis is the same mechanism as P1 — the abstract aligns but full-text check is still pending.
- **Weak measurement backaction**: Halvorsen–Okabe zero-temperature qualification — backaction-free only asymptotically; finite-temperature residual is computed there.

---
